goals.description: Clarify which Docker workflow is requested and gather the relevant project artifacts, such as Dockerfile, compose files, runtime language, services, images, and security targets.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Identify the user's requested Docker work: Dockerfile optimization, compose generation/improvement, security audit, or a combination. Locate the relevant files and project context before entering any specific workflow branch.
goals.name: Determine Docker task scope

goals.description: Inspect the current Dockerfile for base image choice, approximate size implications, layer count, build ordering, and common Docker anti-patterns.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on Dockerfile optimization analysis. If Dockerfile optimization is not in scope, mark this goal not applicable. Read the Dockerfile, identify the base image, count RUN/COPY/ADD layers, and note anti-patterns that affect size, speed, cacheability, or production readiness.
goals.name: Analyze Dockerfile state

goals.description: Choose a production-appropriate base image strategy using specific tags, slim/alpine/distroless variants where suitable, digest pinning for reproducibility when appropriate, and runtime-matched images.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on the base image decision for the optimized Dockerfile. Avoid :latest for production, prefer minimal variants when compatible, consider digest pinning for CI reproducibility, and ensure the base matches the actual runtime needs.
goals.name: Optimize base image

goals.description: Ensure unnecessary files are excluded from the image build context, especially through a .dockerignore that covers source-control, dependency, cache, and secret files.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on build context hygiene. Check whether .dockerignore exists and is sufficient. Add or improve it to exclude files such as .git, dependency directories, caches, bytecode, local environment files, and other unnecessary or sensitive content.
goals.name: Improve Docker build context

goals.description: Reorder and combine Dockerfile instructions to improve layer caching, install dependencies before copying volatile source code, clean package-manager caches in the same layer, and use BuildKit cache mounts where relevant.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on Dockerfile layer and cache behavior. Reorder dependency manifests before source copies, separate dependency installation from app code, combine related RUN commands, clean package-manager caches in the same RUN layer, and consider BuildKit cache mounts where appropriate.
goals.name: Optimize Docker layers and cache

goals.description: Introduce or refine multi-stage builds so build tools and development dependencies stay in builder stages while the final runtime image contains only required production artifacts.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on multi-stage build design when it is relevant. Use a builder stage with SDK/build tools and a minimal runtime stage. Copy only required artifacts with COPY --from, and keep build tools, source code, and development dependencies out of the final image.
goals.name: Apply multi-stage build pattern

goals.description: Produce the optimized Dockerfile using the relevant base-image, build-context, layer-cache, and multi-stage decisions, with inline comments and an estimated size-reduction summary.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Create the optimized Dockerfile from the prior optimization decisions. Apply only relevant improvements, include concise inline comments explaining important choices, and report the expected or estimated size/build improvement when possible.
goals.name: Generate optimized Dockerfile

goals.description: Run or recommend the Dockerfile analyzer against the resulting Dockerfile to verify optimization and security findings.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Validate the optimized Dockerfile. Run `python3 scripts/dockerfile_analyzer.py Dockerfile` if available and appropriate, or clearly state that validation should be run and summarize any remaining warnings.
goals.name: Validate Dockerfile optimization

goals.description: Determine the services needed for docker-compose, including application processes, databases, caches, queues, and reverse proxies, along with their relationships.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on Docker Compose work. If compose generation or improvement is not in scope, mark this goal not applicable. Identify required services such as web/API/worker, database, cache, queue, and reverse proxy, plus their dependencies and exposed interfaces.
goals.name: Identify compose services

goals.description: Apply service-level compose best practices such as healthchecks, depends_on health conditions, resource limits, named volumes for persistent data, and pinned image versions.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on service reliability and operational settings in docker-compose. Add healthchecks, use depends_on with service_healthy where supported, set memory/CPU limits when appropriate, use named volumes for persistent data, and pin image versions.
goals.name: Configure compose service reliability

goals.description: Design explicit compose networks, separate frontend and backend traffic where useful, restrict externally exposed ports, and mark backend-only networks internal.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on Docker Compose networking. Avoid relying solely on the default network when a clearer topology is needed. Separate frontend/backend networks as appropriate, expose only required external ports, and use internal networks for backend-only services.
goals.name: Configure compose networking

goals.description: Move secrets and environment configuration into env files or variable substitutions, ensure .env is ignored, and document required variables in .env.example.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on environment and secret handling for compose. Prefer env_file and variable substitution over inline secrets, ensure real .env files are not committed, and prepare documented placeholders for required variables in .env.example.
goals.name: Configure compose environment handling

goals.description: Differentiate development and production behavior using profiles or override files, with dev conveniences separated from production-safe defaults.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on development versus production compose behavior. Use profiles or override files where useful. Keep bind mounts, hot reload, and debug ports in dev-only configuration; keep production free of debug ports and use suitable restart behavior.
goals.name: Configure compose dev and production modes

goals.description: Produce docker-compose.yml and related environment examples with services, healthchecks, networks, volumes, environment handling, and dev/prod annotations.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Generate or update the compose artifacts. Include docker-compose.yml with the selected services, healthchecks, networks, volumes, and environment configuration. Also generate or update .env.example and annotate dev/prod usage where relevant.
goals.name: Generate compose artifacts

goals.description: Run or recommend the compose validator against the resulting docker-compose.yml to catch dependency, healthcheck, network, volume, environment, and port issues.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Validate the compose file. Run `python3 scripts/compose_validator.py docker-compose.yml` if available and appropriate, or clearly state how validation should be performed and summarize any remaining issues.
goals.name: Validate compose configuration

goals.description: Check Dockerfile-level security issues including root user, latest tags, secrets in ENV or ARG, broad COPY patterns, unnecessary EXPOSE, missing HEALTHCHECK, privileged behavior, and retained package caches.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on Dockerfile security auditing. If security audit is not in scope, mark this goal not applicable. Inspect the Dockerfile for root execution, unpinned/latest images, baked secrets, broad COPY, unnecessary exposed ports, missing healthchecks, privileged patterns, and package cache retention.
goals.name: Audit Dockerfile security

goals.description: Check runtime and compose/container controls such as non-root execution, read-only root filesystem, capability dropping, resource limits, network mode, sensitive mounts, and log size limits.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on runtime container security. Inspect compose files, run configuration, or supplied container settings for root runtime user, writable root filesystem, excessive capabilities, missing resource limits, host networking, sensitive mounts such as docker.sock, and missing log limits.
goals.name: Audit runtime container security

goals.description: Summarize security findings by severity with counts and detailed fix recommendations for Dockerfile and runtime issues.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Prepare the container security audit report. Include severity counts for critical, high, medium, and low findings, and provide concrete remediation recommendations for each Dockerfile or runtime issue found.
goals.name: Generate security report
